newsitem.title: UK: Waste Management to sell Wessex Water shares.
newsitem.headline: Waste Management to sell Wessex Water shares.

text.p: Waste Management International Plc said on Wednesday that it has agreed to sell 87 percent of its 19.5 percent interest in Wessex Water Plc's share capital for a total consideration of not less than 157 million stg in cash.
In said in a statement it also intended to dispose of its remaining 6.5 million ordinary shares in the British water and sewerage firm during 1997.

Waste Management's (WMI) chief executive Joseph Holsten said, "This agreement will position WMI to redeploy cash resources into our core business as we seek to enhance shareholder value and generate higher cash yields over the long term."

Wessex Water announced earlier it had agreed to purchase all of its B and C shares held by Waste Management for 355p per share in cash. Wessex also said it planned a tender offer to buy back 10 percent of its ordinary shares not held by WMI at 380p per share.
As part of the deal, WMI's options to acquire 10.6 million outstanding Wessex ordinary shares will be cancelled.

WMI said that the share sales would result in a fourth quarter charge of around 18.5 million stg before tax, 37.5 million after tax, assuming a sale price of 355p per share for the shares sold to parties other than Wessex.
It said that its net income after tax will be reduced by around 14 million in 1997 as a result of the reduction in equity income from the investment in Wessex.
